Incoming longwave radiation

Source: R/metric-radiation.R
ef_rl_in.Rd

Computes the incoming (downwelling) longwave radiation at the surface, \(R_{L\downarrow}\), emitted by the atmosphere treated as a grey body with an effective emissivity and an effective temperature. The result is the rl_in argument of ef_net_radiation().

Usage

ef_rl_in(temperature, atm_emissivity)

Arguments

temperature

Numeric, no default. Effective temperature of the emitting atmosphere [K], > 0. The function is agnostic about which temperature is used: the air temperature at the overpass time (station or regionalised forcing), the surface temperature of the cold anchor pixel (a scene scalar) or the surface temperature of each pixel. The choice is open (decision RC-12) and must be made, and recorded, by the caller.

atm_emissivity

Numeric. Effective atmospheric emissivity \(\varepsilon_a\) [-], > 0 (e.g. ef_atm_emissivity()). Values above 1 are accepted and reported by the diagnostics of the stage (EF_RAD_ATM_EMISSIVITY_GT1).

Value

A numeric vector of \(R_{L\downarrow}\) [W m-2] with the common length and dim of the inputs.

Details

$$R_{L\downarrow} = \varepsilon_a \sigma T^4$$ with \(\sigma\) the Stefan-Boltzmann constant (CODATA 2018 exact value, 5.670374419e-8 W m-2 K-4, decision RC-07).

Choice of the temperature (RC-12): with the air temperature, the meteorological forcing (and GWR) enters the incoming longwave radiation; with the cold-pixel surface temperature, the result is uniform in the scene except through the emissivity; with the surface temperature of each pixel, hot and dry pixels receive more longwave radiation, which artificially reduces the contrast of net radiation. With which temperature the coefficients of ef_atm_emissivity() were derived is not known (TODO).

Assumptions: grey-body atmosphere with effective emissivity and temperature; clear sky; instantaneous value.

Arguments must be numeric and have length 1 or a common length (a scalar temperature is recycled); matrix or array arguments must share their dim. Non-positive or infinite values raise earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error). Missing values propagate.

Verification status

CANDIDATA. Stefan-Boltzmann law with an effective emissivity, form observed in the water package (v1.0), attributed there to Allen et al. (2007) (equation number and prescribed temperature not verified).

References

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

See also

Other radiation functions: ef_atm_emissivity(), ef_net_radiation(), ef_rl_out(), ef_rs_in(), ef_solar_geometry(), ef_tau_sw()

Examples

# Air temperature of 20 degrees C (293.15 K), transmissivity 0.75
ef_rl_in(temperature = 293.15, atm_emissivity = ef_atm_emissivity(0.75))
#> [1] 318.1943

# A scalar temperature recycled over several pixels
ef_rl_in(temperature = 290, atm_emissivity = c(0.72, 0.75, 0.78))
#> [1] 288.7595 300.7911 312.8228
